paras.text: Super-Cram: The Numbers
This is the last-hour listen. Every number here comes straight from the corpus. Breathe, listen, and let them land one more time.
Licensing law

The law is Article twenty four of the Occupational Code, Public Act two ninety nine of nineteen eighty, M C L three thirty nine point two four zero one through two four one two. The board has nine members: four residential builders, two M and A contractors, three public members. The licensure exemption is six hundred dollars aggregate for labor, materials, and everything else, with an anti-evasion clause — you cannot split jobs. Prelicensure education is sixty hours, at least six hours in each of seven competency areas. The license term is three years. Continuing competency for builders first licensed on or after January first, two thousand nine is at least twenty one hours per three year cycle, with at least three hours each calendar year in the first six years. Builders licensed before two thousand nine with no discipline need only three hours per cycle. Keep continuing competency records five years. You have one year after applying to finish everything, including the exam. A lapsed license under three years costs one hundred eighty five dollars to relicense with no re-education; over three years means the full sixty hours again.

Homeowner complaints must be filed within eighteen months. Notify the department of a change in control within ten days. The administrative fine tops out at ten thousand dollars. Criminal fines for unlicensed building run five thousand to twenty five thousand dollars: up to one year in jail for a first offense, two years for a second, and it becomes a felony with up to four years if the work causes a death. An unlicensed builder cannot sue for payment and cannot record a lien.

Exam vitals: one hundred sixty questions — fifty business and law plus one hundred ten trade. Passing raw score one hundred sixteen, which is seventy two and a half percent, in two hundred forty minutes. Regulatory and statutory requirements is the biggest business and law category at thirteen of fifty. Application fee one ninety five, exam fee one seventeen, salesperson exam eighty five dollars. The exam references the twenty fifteen Michigan Residential Code.
Liens, insurance, and bonds

Subcontractors and suppliers serve the Notice of Furnishing within twenty days of first furnishing. Laborers get thirty days from when unpaid wages were due. A homeowner has ten days to return a requested Notice of Commencement. Record the claim of lien within ninety days after your last furnishing — warranty and punch-list work do not restart the clock. Serve a copy within fifteen days of recording. File the foreclosure suit within one year of recording, in circuit court, or the lien dies. There are four lien waiver types: full and partial, each conditional or unconditional. A conditional waiver is effective only when payment actually clears. Residential lien rights require a written contract with the licensure statement and license number, at any dollar amount. The Homeowner Construction Lien Recovery Fund was abolished in twenty ten — any answer relying on it is wrong.

Public projects over fifty thousand dollars require performance and payment bonds, each at least twenty five percent of the contract amount. The performance bond protects the governmental unit; the payment bond protects subs, suppliers, and laborers. Bond claimants without privity give notice within thirty days after first furnishing and again within ninety days after last furnishing.

Workers comp is required with three or more employees at one time, or one employee working thirty five plus hours a week for thirteen or more weeks in the preceding fifty two. A general contractor is liable for comp claims of an uninsured sub's injured workers. Builders risk covers the structure and materials; C G L covers third-party injury and damage, never your own defective work.
Contracts and consumer law

HIFA triggers when the cash price exceeds three hundred dollars on installment credit — exactly three hundred is excluded. HIFA rescission runs to five p m of the next business day. The Home Solicitation Sales Act cancellation runs to midnight of the third business day, and after cancellation the seller refunds within ten business days and has twenty days to pick up goods. HIFA type sizes: eight point body, ten point bold headings. Willful HIFA violation: ninety days and or five hundred dollars.

Statutes of limitation: breach of contract, six years. Negligence, three years. The statute of repose for construction defects is six years from occupancy, use, or acceptance; the gross negligence exception allows one year after discovery with an absolute cap of ten years. Retainage typically runs five to ten percent.
Business management

Michigan sales tax is six percent — contractors pay it on materials; installation labor is exempt. Markup is not margin: twenty five percent markup is a twenty percent margin; the ten and ten formula is really sixteen point six seven percent margin. To get a twenty percent margin, divide cost by point eight zero. FICA is six point two percent Social Security plus one point four five percent Medicare — seven point six five percent each side. FUTA is six percent on the first seven thousand dollars, netting to point six percent. Overtime is time and a half over forty hours in a workweek. The ten ninety nine N E C threshold for twenty twenty six payments is two thousand dollars, up from six hundred. The L L C annual statement is due February fifteenth with a twenty five dollar fee. New construction employers pay the construction industry average unemployment rate, not the standard two point seven percent. Keep the MIOSHA three hundred log if you have eleven or more employees; post the three hundred A summary February first through April thirtieth.
Safety

Fall protection at six feet. Guardrail top rail at forty two inches plus or minus three, withstanding two hundred pounds. Scaffold guardrails trigger at ten feet, and scaffolds carry four times the intended load. Ladders: four to one pitch, three feet above the landing, rungs ten to fourteen inches apart, twenty feet from power lines for a portable ladder — ten feet is the equipment clearance up to fifty k V. Trenches: protective system at five feet, ladder at four feet within twenty five feet of travel, spoil piles two feet back, engineer design at twenty feet. Soil slopes: Type A is three quarters to one at fifty three degrees, Type B one to one at forty five degrees, Type C one and a half to one at thirty four degrees — Type C can never be benched. Silica limit is fifty micrograms per cubic meter with an action level of twenty five. Construction noise limit: ninety d B A. Report a fatality within eight hours; hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within twenty four. Serious violation penalty: up to seven thousand dollars; willful or repeat, up to seventy thousand. Call MISS DIG at eight one one three full working days before digging; the fine is up to five thousand dollars.
Footings, foundations, concrete

Michigan frost depth: forty two inches. Footings: six inches thick minimum, projecting at least two inches each side but never more than their own thickness. Anchor bolts: half inch diameter, six feet on center, seven inches embedded, two per plate, within twelve inches of plate ends. Grade slopes away six inches in the first ten feet. Foundation walls extend four inches above grade with veneer, six inches otherwise. Drain gravel goes one foot beyond the footing and six inches above it. Concrete strengths: twenty five hundred p s i for footings and interior work, three thousand for exposed vertical, thirty five hundred for garage slabs, porches, and steps. Air content five to seven percent. Slab on grade: three and a half inches thick on a four inch base with six mil poly. Rebar cover against earth: three inches, steel in the bottom third of the footing. Concrete hits about seventy percent strength at seven days, design strength at twenty eight. Soil bearing: clay fifteen hundred, sand two thousand, sandy gravel three thousand, sedimentary rock four thousand pounds per square foot. Crawl space vents: one to one fifty; floor access eighteen by twenty four, wall access sixteen by twenty four. Septic tank minimum one thousand gallons, fifty feet to the well.
Carpentry

Joist bearing: one and a half inches on wood or metal, three inches on masonry or concrete. Bridging only for joists deeper than two by twelve. Joist cuts: notch depth one sixth, end notch one quarter, holes and notch length one third, with two inches of clearance — no notches in the middle third. Studs: notch twenty five percent bearing, forty percent nonbearing; bore forty percent bearing, sixty percent nonbearing or doubled. A top plate cut over fifty percent gets a sixteen gauge tie, one and a half inches wide, eight ten-penny nails. Two by four bearing studs: twenty four inches on center for roof and ceiling only, sixteen for one floor plus roof; two floors plus roof means two by six. Top plate joints offset twenty four inches. Double the header and trimmers when a floor opening exceeds four feet. Ridge board one inch nominal; hips and valleys two inch nominal; below three in twelve the ridge is a designed beam. Collar ties in the upper third, one by four, four feet on center — rafter ties, not collar ties, resist thrust. Nailing: top plate to top plate sixteen penny at sixteen inches; joists toenailed with three eight-penny nails; sheathing at six inches on edges, twelve in the field.

Michigan stairs: maximum riser eight and a quarter inches, minimum tread nine inches, variation three eighths of an inch, headroom six feet eight, width thirty six inches, handrail thirty four to thirty eight inches on flights of four or more risers. Guards at thirty six inches where you can fall more than thirty inches, rejecting a four inch sphere. Deck ledger: two by eight pressure treated with half inch hot-dipped galvanized lags or bolts, lateral hold-downs of fifteen hundred pounds at two locations, and deck footings at forty two inches.
Masonry, roofing, siding

Mortar strongest to weakest: M, S, N, O — twenty five hundred, eighteen hundred, seven fifty, three fifty p s i. Type M below grade, Type N for veneer. Veneer air space one inch to four and a half. Ties: thirty two inches horizontal, twenty four vertical, two point six seven square feet each. Weeps at thirty three inches, three sixteenths inch minimum, above the flashing. Lintels bear four inches each end. Firebox: twenty inches deep, ten inch walls or eight with firebrick. Hearth four inches, extension two; extensions sixteen front and eight sides, or twenty and twelve at six square feet and up. Chimney: three feet above the roof penetration and two feet above anything within ten feet; cricket required over thirty inches wide. Flue ratios: one twelfth round, one tenth square, one eighth for narrow rectangles. Chimney clearance two inches interior, one inch exterior.

Shingles: minimum slope two in twelve, double underlayment below four in twelve, four nails per strip. Ice barrier runs twenty four inches inside the exterior wall line — not from the eave edge. Drip edge: quarter inch below sheathing, two inches onto the deck. Step flashing four by four. Open valley metal twenty four inches wide. Tear off at two existing layers. Attic vent one to one fifty, dropping to one to three hundred with a qualifying condition; keep a one inch baffle airspace.
Envelope and interior

Insulation: ceiling R thirty eight in zone five A, R forty nine in six A and seven. Walls R twenty, or R thirteen plus five continuous. Window U factor point three two, skylight point five five. Air leakage four A C H fifty with a blower door test. Vapor retarder Class one or two on the interior side. Bath exhaust fifty c f m intermittent or twenty continuous; kitchen one hundred or twenty five. Egress windows: five point seven square feet — five even at grade floor — twenty four inches high, twenty wide, sill no more than forty four inches. Window wells nine square feet with thirty six inch projection. Safety glazing within a twenty four inch arc of doors below sixty inches, and the four-part big-pane rule: nine square feet, eighteen, thirty six, thirty six. Garage separation: half inch gypsum on walls, five eighths Type X on ceilings under habitable space; the house door is one and three eighths inches solid or twenty minute rated, self-closing. Attic access twenty two by thirty. Radon action level four picocuries per liter.
Plans, math, permits

Floor plans: quarter inch equals one foot. Window three zero five zero means three feet wide, five feet high. Board feet: thickness times width times length in feet, divided by twelve. Twenty seven cubic feet per cubic yard. Six point seven five bricks per square foot; one point one two five blocks. A square is one hundred square feet, three bundles. A four by eight sheet is thirty two square feet. Studs at sixteen on center: length times point seven five plus one. Earth swells about twenty five percent loose. Written dimensions always govern over scaling. Permit exemptions: sheds two hundred square feet, fences seven feet, retaining walls four feet, decks two hundred square feet under thirty inches. Permits issue in ten business days, expire after one hundred eighty days idle; certificate of occupancy in five business days. Sealed plans not needed under thirty five hundred square feet. Plumbers: six thousand hours to journeyman, four thousand more to master. Electricians: eight thousand to journeyman, twelve thousand to master.
The ten nastiest traps
One. Frost depth is forty two inches — a Michigan amendment. The generic twelve inch footing answer is wrong here.
Two. Stairs: Michigan allows an eight and a quarter inch riser and nine inch tread. The I R C's seven and three quarters and ten are the trap answers.
Three. Ceiling insulation in zone five A is R thirty eight by Michigan amendment — the base code's R forty nine is the trap for southern Michigan.
Four. Window U factor is point three two. Point three zero is the twenty twenty one code, which never took effect.
Five. The exam tests the twenty fifteen Michigan Residential Code — the twenty twenty one update was stayed and never adopted.
Six. Permit-exempt sheds are two hundred square feet. One hundred twenty is the old-code trap.
Seven. Anchor bolts stay at six feet on center in Michigan — the four foot spacing is a seismic rule for other states.
Eight. MIOSHA's serious violation max is seven thousand dollars by state statute — the sixteen thousand figure is federal.
Nine. The Lien Recovery Fund was abolished in twenty ten. Any answer leaning on it is dead wrong.
Ten. Wood shakes need only three in twelve under the M R C — four in twelve is the commercial code trap.
That is the whole deck. Walk in, find the Michigan number, and pass.
